chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created happiness (sa'adah) and misery (shaqawah) before He created His creation. So whoever Allah knows to be happy, He never hates him, even if he does an evil deed, Allah hates his deed but does not hate him. And if He knows someone to be miserable, He never loves him, even if he does a good deed, Allah loves his deed but hates him for what he will become. Thus, if Allah loves something, He never hates it; and if He hates something, He never loves it.

key_terms.السَّعَادَة: Happiness or blessedness (eternal state of bliss)
key_terms.الشَّقَاوَة: Misery or wretchedness (eternal state of punishment)
key_terms.لِمَا يَصِيرُ إِلَيْهِ: For what he will become (referring to the ultimate outcome of the soul)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's love for a person and His love for their deeds according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the Shia doctrine of *al-Sa'adah wa al-Shaqawah al-Mubramah* (decisive happiness and misery), asserting that Allah’s eternal knowledge pre-determines the ultimate spiritual trajectory of individuals. It distinguishes between Allah’s love for the person versus His love for their specific deeds, illustrating that a 'happy' soul may perform evil but is ultimately beloved, while a 'miserable' soul may perform good but remains destined for loss. This reinforces the interplay between divine foreknowledge and human agency within the framework of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn*.
